aiBridgeSettings.title: AI Interaction Bridge
aiBridgeSettings.enabledDesc: Allows a local AI client to access this instance; control also depends on the permission level.
aiBridgeSettings.permissionDesc: Can be set before enabling. Read-only permits queries; Full control also permits sessions, commands, and configuration changes.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverDesc: Copy the connection prompt to a local AI. The indicator lights after a successful handshake while the connection remains open.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverDialogTitle: Connect an AI to this instance
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverDialogIntro: Copy this prompt to an AI that can access local files and Windows Named Pipes. A browser-only chat cannot connect directly to local software.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverPermissionReadOnly: Current permission: Read-only. The AI can inspect state and logs but cannot send commands or change settings.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverPermissionFullControl: Current permission: Full control. The AI can connect serial ports, send commands, and change settings within the published capability boundary.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverPrompt:
Connect to the currently running SuperConnectX instance. Do not start a second instance.

1. Under %APPDATA%\superconnectx\bridge\, choose endpoint.json or endpoint-*.json whose instance.pid is still running. Read pipeName and token; use the token only for auth and never print it.
2. Under the same local user context as the app, connect to the Windows Named Pipe with UTF-8 (no BOM) NDJSON: call auth first, then immediately call client_hello with clientName. Keep the Pipe open and verify that SuperConnectX reports “AI connected” before operating.
3. Call get_info and get_capabilities, then use only methods exposed by this instance and allowed by its permission gate.
4. Distinguish list_serial_ports (live system ports), list_connections (saved profiles), and list_sessions (running sessions); use the path returned by list_serial_ports as the port identifier.
5. create_connection/update_connection are limited to GUI-exposed Telnet and FTP profiles. Any new AI serial session must be visible in the GUI.
6. tx.accepted means that the software accepted the send; continue reading rx.display, the prompt, or the software log to confirm the device response.
aiBridgeSettings.takeoverPortSessionRule: Normalize a numeric Windows port to the COM-prefixed form (for example, 90 to COM90), then match the path returned by list_serial_ports: call start_port_session when present, or report PORT_NOT_FOUND when absent; use attach_session for an existing session. Never create a saved COM profile or open a port directly.
aiBridgeSettings.promptCopied: Connection prompt copied. Send it to your AI.
aiBridgeSettings.promptCopyFailed: Copy failed. Select and copy the prompt manually.
aiBridgeSettings.feedbackDesc: The overlay shows immediate AI activity. Full records remain in the history and local log when the bridge is off.
aiBridgeSettings.overlayClickableDesc: Clicking an overlay item opens AI activity history; when off, the overlay remains visible but ignores clicks.
aiBridgeSettings.activityHistoryDesc: Shows AI queries and operation results in real time and writes them to a read-only local activity log.

aiBridgeSettings.activityLogDesc: Records are written asynchronously to a dedicated ai-activity directory and rotated by size, preventing unbounded files and main-process blocking.
aiBridgeSettings.activityLogPathDesc: Files are stored in an ai-activity subdirectory below the selected folder. Leave blank to use the application log directory.
aiBridgeSettings.activityLogMaxSizeDesc: The active log rotates to an archive named with a millisecond timestamp.
aiBridgeSettings.activityLogMaxFilesDesc: Includes the active file; the oldest backup is removed when the limit is exceeded.
aiBridgeSettings.capabilityDesc: Exposes sessions, sending, connection profiles, command libraries, and settings needed for serial debugging. Auxiliary features such as themes, virtual ports, and updates are excluded.
aiBridgeSettings.enableRequired: This function requires “AI Interaction Bridge - Enable bridge” to be enabled.
aiBridgeSettings.fullControlRequired: This function requires “AI permission level - Full control” to be enabled.

aiBridgeSettings.docsOverviewText: A local AI client can query this running SuperConnectX instance, reuse sessions in the window, and send commands. Queries return current values on demand; terminal and configuration changes can be streamed as events.
aiBridgeSettings.docsTechnologyText: The bridge runs in the Electron/Node.js main process and accepts local JSON-RPC 2.0 requests over a Windows Named Pipe. The endpoint file contains only the pipe address and a random token; live state comes from responses and runtime events. Serial, configuration, and storage actions use the application's internal shared services.
aiBridgeSettings.docsPlatformText: The bridge uses the current user account. It starts no elevated process and uses no screen, mouse, or keyboard automation. It relies on Node.js built-ins net, fs, and crypto, with no AI-specific third-party library. Windows Named Pipe is the current transport; protocol and business services can be reused by another local IPC adapter.
aiBridgeSettings.docsPermissionText: When disabled, every request except token authentication is rejected. Read-only permits session, configuration, and recent terminal-event queries. Full control also permits connection lifecycle, sending, and configuration writes. Every request still passes capability and field validation.
aiBridgeSettings.docsOperationText: AI connections create visible tabs, transmissions appear as AI SEND in the matching terminal, and configuration changes refresh the UI. Commands use the current newline, HEX, and CRC settings without taking over the active tab, input box, or command group.
aiBridgeSettings.docsSafetyText: Keep the bridge off for normal use and prefer Read-only for diagnosis. Enable Full control only for sending or configuration changes, then verify results in AI SEND records, activity history, and the local activity log.
